addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Use when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing models (Claude, Llama, [infra], Titan). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.

Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. content.content:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/eikek/docspell
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghcr.io/docspell/restserver:v0.43.0 (plus ghcr.io/docspell/joex:v0.43.0)
  port: 7880
  vm: m1.large
  flavor_id: "4"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.066
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: docspell
quirks:
  - "⛔ READ THE DISK NUMBERS TO THE USER BEFORE YOU SIZE ANYTHING, BECAUSE DOCSPELL PUTS THE DOCUMENTS IN THE DATABASE. files.default-store defaults to \"database\" in BOTH components (restserver reference.conf ~469, joex reference.conf ~759) and upstream calls that the recommended default. So every scanned PDF, every converted PDF/A, every extracted preview image and every archived original is stored as blobs in the managed Postgres, NOT on the app VM. The consequence: the MANAGED DATABASE flavor's disk is your archive size cap. m1.small gives 20 GB, m1.medium 40 GB for GBP 0.0104/hr more, m1.large 80 GB. The app VM's 80 GB holds only Ubuntu, docker and the two images. Say those numbers out loud before the plan is approved: growing the database VM later is a volume resize, not a redeploy. Docspell keeps the original AND a converted PDF AND previews for each upload, so budget roughly two to three times the raw scan size."
  - "⛔ THE COMPOSE IS IN A DIFFERENT REPO, AND THE ONE IN THE MAIN REPO IS AN SMTP DEMO. eikek/docspell contains exactly one docker-compose.yml, at tools/exim/docker-compose.yml, and it is an exim mail relay on host networking publishing port 25. It does not contain Docspell and it must never be deployed here. The real stack is docspell/docker (branch main) at docker-compose/docker-compose.yml. Adapt THAT one, and delete three of its five services as described below."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY, BECAUSE DOCSPELL HAS NO INSTANCE ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT AT ALL, AND THAT IS WHY THE DEFAULT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN SAFE. Every sign-up creates a COLLECTIVE (a tenant) with one user inside it, and backend.signup.mode defaults to \"open\" (restserver reference.conf ~425-435). So this is not a first-one-wins race like most apps: with the default, EVERYONE wins, forever. Anybody who finds the hostname creates their own collective, uploads documents into your Postgres and burns your OCR CPU, and nothing in the product can evict them. THE FIX IS A DEPLOY-TIME ONE AND IT LEAVES NO WINDOW: set DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_SIGNUP_MODE=invite and DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_SIGNUP_NEW__INVITE__PASSWORD to a generated alphanumeric value BEFORE first boot. Verified in OSignup.scala:49-83 that invite mode rejects a registration with no valid invite key for every registration including the very first, and at :38-47 that minting a key requires the configured password to be non-empty and to match exactly. Then, after the container is healthy, POST {\"password\":\"[REDACTED:value]\"} to /api/v1/open/signup/newinvite, take the id it returns, and register your own account with it via /api/v1/open/signup/register. Do NOT use mode=closed to \"be safe\": it refuses you too, and you would have to redeploy to get in."
  - "IS REGISTRATION OPEN AFTER YOUR ACCOUNT EXISTS? In invite mode, only to somebody holding a key you minted, and keys are single-use with a default validity of 3 days. That is already closed in practice. The belt-and-braces step, once you are in, is to redeploy with DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_SIGNUP_MODE=closed, which is a container restart and costs nothing. Ask the user which they want rather than deciding for them: a family archive usually wants invite, a single-person archive wants closed."
  - "⛔⛔ DO NOT COPY THE ADMIN SECRET OUT OF THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE. IT IS A PUBLISHED VALUE AND IT UNLOCKS PASSWORD RESET FOR EVERY ACCOUNT. docspell/docker's compose sets DOCSPELL_SERVER_ADMIN__ENDPOINT_SECRET to a short hardcoded string that appears in a public repo and in every tutorial derived from it. Anyone who sends it in a Docspell-Admin-Secret header can call POST /api/v1/admin/user/resetPassword and take over any collective on the instance, plus reset OTP, re-index and clone the file repository. The default in reference.conf (~315-317) is EMPTY, which disables every /api/v1/admin route, and empty is what this recipe ships. If the user genuinely wants the admin routes later, generate a fresh long alphanumeric value; never the upstream one."
  - "⛔ DISABLE THE INTEGRATION ENDPOINT, WHICH THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE TURNS ON. It sets DOCSPELL_SERVER_INTEGRATION__ENDPOINT_ENABLED=true with a hardcoded header value, because its consumedir container needs it. That endpoint is POST /api/v1/open/integration/item/<collective>, it is anonymous by design, and the header value protecting it is published in the same file everyone copies. On a private LAN that is a reasonable trade; on a public *.redu.cloud hostname it is an anonymous upload endpoint into your database with a known password. reference.conf's own comment (~255-269) says \"If all protection methods are disabled, the endpoint is not protected at all!\". Set it to false, and drop the consumedir container that wanted it."
  - "⛔ DELETE THREE OF THE FIVE UPSTREAM SERVICES. (1) `db`, its bundled postgres:18.6, or you run two databases and the app talks to the wrong one. (2) `consumedir`, the dsc watcher: it bind-mounts ./docs from the project directory, which is exactly what a source re-upload replaces, and it exists only to feed the integration endpoint you just disabled. Upload through the web UI or the API instead. (3) `solr`, for the reason in the next quirk. What remains is restserver and joex."
  - "SOLR CAN BE DROPPED WITHOUT LOSING FULL-TEXT SEARCH, AND THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST SAVING IN THE RECIPE. Docspell supports two full-text backends, solr and postgresql (restserver reference.conf ~321-350). The PostgreSQL one creates exactly ONE table, ftspsql_search, with a generated tsvector column and a GIN index, and needs no extension at all: verified by reading modules/fts-psql/src/main/resources/db/psqlfts/V2.0.0__initial_schema.sql, which contains no CREATE EXTENSION, no unaccent and no pg_trgm. So set, on BOTH components, FULL__TEXT__SEARCH_ENABLED=true, FULL__TEXT__SEARCH_BACKEND=postgresql and FULL__TEXT__SEARCH_POSTGRESQL_USE__DEFAULT__CONNECTION=true, and the index lives in the managed database you are already paying for. That removes a third JVM and a second stateful volume from the app VM. The trade is real and worth stating: upstream says query features differ between backends, so a content query written for Solr may not behave identically. Solr remains the documented alternative for anyone who wants it, at the cost of m1.mem16 instead of m1.large."
  - "⛔ THE FULL-TEXT CONFIG MUST BE IDENTICAL ON BOTH COMPONENTS. reference.conf says so in both files (\"the same must be used for joex\" / \"for restserver\"). Setting it on the restserver only gives you a search box that returns nothing, because joex is what writes the index, and nothing errors."
  - "⛔ WITHOUT THE JDBC VARIABLES BOTH CONTAINERS COME UP HEALTHY ON SEPARATE THROWAWAY H2 DATABASES IN /tmp. Both reference.conf files default jdbc.url to jdbc:h2:// plus the JVM's temp directory plus /docspell-demo.db (restserver ~401, joex ~49). The failure is worse than the usual SQLite fallback because the two containers do not share /tmp: the restserver gets one database, joex gets another, so you can sign up, log in, upload a document, and watch it sit in processing forever while every screen looks correct. Set all three on EACH component: DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL / _USER / _PASSWORD and DOCSPELL_JOEX_JDBC_URL / _USER / _PASSWORD. deploy_compose with database:'managed' only APPENDS PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/DATABASE_URL to the project .env, it never edits your compose, so the compose must interpolate them itself: DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL: \"jdbc:postgresql://${PGHOST}:[REDACTED:conn-password]/${PGDATABASE}\", _USER: \"${PGUSER}\", _PASSWORD: \"${PGPASSWORD}\". Docspell does NOT read DATABASE_URL: the JDBC url has its own scheme and no credentials in it."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, NEVER BY ABSENCE ALONE. On the app VM: `sudo docker exec docspell-restserver printenv DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL` must print a jdbc:postgresql:// url pointing at the private database IP. That is the positive half and it is also what tells you the exec worked at all. THEN `sudo docker exec docspell-restserver ls /tmp` must show NO docspell-demo.db. If the first command errored, the second one's silence means nothing. Repeat both for docspell-joex. The VM runs docker, not podman."
  - "⛔ SET DOCSPELL_SERVER_AUTH_SERVER__SECRET EXPLICITLY AND REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY. It ships EMPTY in reference.conf (~87) and the comment beside it says a random secret is generated when it is empty, so every container restart silently invalidates every session AND every remember-me token, which are valid for 30 days by default. Nobody loses data and nothing errors; everyone is just logged out, repeatedly, for no visible reason. Generate one long random value and pass it with the b64: or hex: prefix the config documents. To be precise about what this is and is not: it signs authentication tokens. It does not encrypt anything at rest, and Docspell has no separate data-encryption key, so there is nothing here that a lost secret makes unrecoverable."
  - "⛔ BOTH COMPONENTS BIND TO localhost BY DEFAULT. restserver reference.conf ~44 and joex ~16-18 both set bind.address = \"localhost\", which inside a container means nothing outside that container can reach it. Set DOCSPELL_SERVER_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0 and DOCSPELL_JOEX_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0. The upstream compose does this and it is easy to lose when you trim the file."
  - "THE TWO CONTAINERS HAVE TO FIND EACH OTHER, AND THE SYMPTOM OF GETTING IT WRONG IS DOCUMENTS THAT NEVER PROCESS. Set DOCSPELL_SERVER_INTERNAL__URL=http://docspell-restserver:7880 and DOCSPELL_JOEX_BASE__URL=http://docspell-joex:7878, using the compose service hostnames. joex registers itself at its base-url so the restserver can poke it when a job arrives; if that url is wrong the job still runs, but only when the scheduler next polls, so it looks like extreme slowness rather than a misconfiguration."
  - "⛔ DO NOT PUBLISH joex's PORT 7878. The upstream compose maps it to the host because it assumes a private LAN. It is a small unauthenticated HTTP API for inspecting and cancelling jobs, and it has no business on the VM's host interface. Expose ONLY the restserver's 7880 to redu's proxy, and give joex no ports: entry at all. Container-to-container traffic on the compose network does not need a published port."
  - "SET DOCSPELL_SERVER_BASE__URL TO THE PUBLIC HTTPS ORIGIN, AND GENERATE THE DNAME YOURSELF FIRST. Left at its default, Docspell reconstructs the external url from X-Forwarded-* and Host headers on every request, which mostly works and fails in exactly the places that are hard to debug: the auth cookie's Secure and domain attributes, and absolute links in notification e-mails. Generate the hostname up front in the full docspell-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form (a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match) and set DOCSPELL_SERVER_BASE__URL=https://<that>. Leave DOCSPELL_JOEX_BASE__URL on the internal container name; it is a different url for a different purpose."
  - "⛔ A HEALTHY DOCSPELL ANSWERS 303 ON /, NOT 200. RestServer.scala:121 mounts GET / as a See Other to /app. A poller that only accepts 200 on / will run its whole timeout against an instance that has been healthy for minutes. Use GET /api/info/version, which is anonymous, returns JSON containing builtAtString, and proves the restserver is actually running rather than that a page rendered."

# Self-host Docspell on redu

Scan a pile of paper into one searchable archive that you own: OCR, automatic tagging and
full-text search, on your own VM, with the documents in a managed Postgres beside it.

## What this deploys

- **Docspell restserver** from the official pinned image, on one m1.large VM, port 7880.
- **Docspell joex**, the worker that does OCR, PDF conversion and text analysis, on the same VM
  and not exposed to the internet.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the metadata, the full-text index **and the
  document files themselves**.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Docspell on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The number to decide on before you deploy: disk

Docspell stores the **files** in the database, not on the app VM. That is upstream's recommended
default and it is genuinely convenient, because one backup covers everything and deleting the
deployment cannot lose a document. It also means the **managed database flavor's disk is your
archive size cap**:

| Managed Postgres | Disk | Extra per hour |
|---|---|---|
| m1.small (default here) | 20 GB | included in the quote |
| m1.medium | 40 GB | +GBP 0.0104 |
| m1.large | 80 GB | +GBP 0.0312 |

Docspell keeps the original file, a converted PDF and preview images for each upload, so budget
roughly two to three times the raw size of what you scan. Growing it later is a volume resize,
not a redeploy, so pick with that in mind.

## The four that actually break it

**Signup is open by default, and Docspell has no instance administrator.** Every sign-up creates
its own tenant, so the default is not a race that someone wins, it is a door that stays open.
The recipe sets signup to *invite* with a generated invite password before first boot, which
closes it with no window at all.

**The admin secret in the upstream compose is a published value.** Anyone who sends it can reset
the password of any account on the instance. This recipe leaves it empty, which disables the
admin routes entirely.

**Without the JDBC variables, both containers start on separate throwaway H2 databases in
`/tmp`.** You can sign up, log in and upload, and the document sits in processing forever
because the worker is looking at a different database.

**Solr is optional.** Docspell can put the full-text index in the Postgres you are already
paying for, which removes a third JVM from the VM. That is what this recipe does.

## Check it before you hand the URL to anyone

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It proves it is talking to Docspell **before** it
asserts anything, because redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for roughly the first
2.5 minutes while the containers start, and an error page fails to register just as convincingly
as a locked instance does.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a fresh Docspell is not open for registration.
#   ./verify-docspell.sh docspell-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = NOT closed, 2 = inconclusive (retry; it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-docspell.sh <host>.redu.cloud}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. Everything below is vacuous unless Docspell itself is answering.
#    Note / is a 303 to /app on a HEALTHY instance, so this uses the JSON endpoint instead.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/info/version" || echo 000)
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info/version answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ]; then
    echo "  That is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"builtAtString"' "$TMP/ver"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200, but the body is not Docspell's VersionInfo." >&2
  echo "  Something else is answering on this hostname. Do not read this as closed." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK   Docspell is answering: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL for step 3. A route that exists but rejects the method answers 405;
#    a route that is not registered answers 404. Without this, a moved endpoint would make
#    step 3 pass for the wrong reason.
probe=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
if [ "$probe" != "405" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: GET on the register route answered $probe, expected 405." >&2
  echo "  The signup API has moved. Step 3 would prove nothing. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK   the register route is where this recipe expects it (GET -> 405)"

# 3. THE NEGATIVE, and it means something now: a registration with no invite key is refused.
probe_name="probe$(date +%s)"
probe_pw=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)
out=$(printf '{"collectiveName":"%s","login":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
        "$probe_name" "$probe_name" "$probe_pw" \
      | curl -sS -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
             "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
case "$out" in
  *'"success":false'*)
    echo "OK   anonymous signup refused: $out" ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL: anonymous signup was NOT refused: $out" >&2
    echo "  Signup mode is not 'invite'. Anyone who finds this URL can create a tenant on it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

echo
echo "Still to do on the VM, and both halves matter:"
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver printenv DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL"
echo "    positive: must print a jdbc:postgresql:// url at the private database IP."
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver ls /tmp"
echo "    negative: must NOT list docspell-demo.db, which is the H2 fallback."
echo "  If the first command errors, the second one's silence proves nothing."
```

## Licence, since it is a fair question

Docspell is **AGPL-3.0-or-later**, not the GPL-3.0 that several directories list. For a
self-hoster running the official images that changes nothing. If you modify Docspell and let
other people use your modified copy over a network, section 13 says you have to offer them the
source of your changes. Running it yourself, unmodified, triggers none of that, and redu is not
the operator: the instance is yours, in your own account.

# Self-host Docspell on redu

Scan a pile of paper into one searchable archive that you own: OCR, automatic tagging and
full-text search, on your own VM, with the documents in a managed Postgres beside it.

## What this deploys

- **Docspell restserver** from the official pinned image, on one m1.large VM, port 7880.
- **Docspell joex**, the worker that does OCR, PDF conversion and text analysis, on the same VM
  and not exposed to the internet.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the metadata, the full-text index **and the
  document files themselves**.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Docspell on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The number to decide on before you deploy: disk

Docspell stores the **files** in the database, not on the app VM. That is upstream's recommended
default and it is genuinely convenient, because one backup covers everything and deleting the
deployment cannot lose a document. It also means the **managed database flavor's disk is your
archive size cap**:

| Managed Postgres | Disk | Extra per hour |
|---|---|---|
| m1.small (default here) | 20 GB | included in the quote |
| m1.medium | 40 GB | +GBP 0.0104 |
| m1.large | 80 GB | +GBP 0.0312 |

Docspell keeps the original file, a converted PDF and preview images for each upload, so budget
roughly two to three times the raw size of what you scan. Growing it later is a volume resize,
not a redeploy, so pick with that in mind.

## The four that actually break it

**Signup is open by default, and Docspell has no instance administrator.** Every sign-up creates
its own tenant, so the default is not a race that someone wins, it is a door that stays open.
The recipe sets signup to *invite* with a generated invite password before first boot, which
closes it with no window at all.

**The admin secret in the upstream compose is a published value.** Anyone who sends it can reset
the password of any account on the instance. This recipe leaves it empty, which disables the
admin routes entirely.

**Without the JDBC variables, both containers start on separate throwaway H2 databases in
`/tmp`.** You can sign up, log in and upload, and the document sits in processing forever
because the worker is looking at a different database.

**Solr is optional.** Docspell can put the full-text index in the Postgres you are already
paying for, which removes a third JVM from the VM. That is what this recipe does.

## Check it before you hand the URL to anyone

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It proves it is talking to Docspell **before** it
asserts anything, because redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for roughly the first
2.5 minutes while the containers start, and an error page fails to register just as convincingly
as a locked instance does.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a fresh Docspell is not open for registration.
#   ./verify-docspell.sh docspell-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = NOT closed, 2 = inconclusive (retry; it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-docspell.sh <host>.redu.cloud}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. Everything below is vacuous unless Docspell itself is answering.
#    Note / is a 303 to /app on a HEALTHY instance, so this uses the JSON endpoint instead.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/info/version" || echo 000)
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info/version answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ]; then
    echo "  That is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"builtAtString"' "$TMP/ver"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200, but the body is not Docspell's VersionInfo." >&2
  echo "  Something else is answering on this hostname. Do not read this as closed." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK   Docspell is answering: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL for step 3. A route that exists but rejects the method answers 405;
#    a route that is not registered answers 404. Without this, a moved endpoint would make
#    step 3 pass for the wrong reason.
probe=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
if [ "$probe" != "405" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: GET on the register route answered $probe, expected 405." >&2
  echo "  The signup API has moved. Step 3 would prove nothing. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK   the register route is where this recipe expects it (GET -> 405)"

# 3. THE NEGATIVE, and it means something now: a registration with no invite key is refused.
probe_name="probe$(date +%s)"
probe_pw=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)
out=$(printf '{"collectiveName":"%s","login":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
        "$probe_name" "$probe_name" "$probe_pw" \
      | curl -sS -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
             "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
case "$out" in
  *'"success":false'*)
    echo "OK   anonymous signup refused: $out" ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL: anonymous signup was NOT refused: $out" >&2
    echo "  Signup mode is not 'invite'. Anyone who finds this URL can create a tenant on it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

echo
echo "Still to do on the VM, and both halves matter:"
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver printenv DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL"
echo "    positive: must print a jdbc:postgresql:// url at the private database IP."
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver ls /tmp"
echo "    negative: must NOT list docspell-demo.db, which is the H2 fallback."
echo "  If the first command errors, the second one's silence proves nothing."
```

## Licence, since it is a fair question

Docspell is **AGPL-3.0-or-later**, not the GPL-3.0 that several directories list. For a
self-hoster running the official images that changes nothing. If you modify Docspell and let
other people use your modified copy over a network, section 13 says you have to offer them the
source of your changes. Running it yourself, unmodified, triggers none of that, and redu is not
the operator: the instance is yours, in your own account.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and corrects anything above that turned out to be wrong. The three most useful
  things it can add are a steady-state memory figure, because upstream publishes only JVM heap
  numbers, how long the roughly 2.4 GB of compressed image layers actually take to pull, and how
  much of the database VM's 20 GB a first batch of scans really costs.

A MANAGED DATABASE IS A SECOND VM WITH ITS OWN HOURLY RATE, and delete_deployment deliberately LEAVES IT BEHIND so your data survives the app. That means a teardown that stops at delete_deployment keeps billing a database nobody can reach. Call delete_database too, and say so to the user before either.

A MANAGED POSTGRES SERVES EXACTLY ONE DATABASE. pg_hba is evaluated before role privileges, so being superuser does not help. An app that wants a second database needs a second managed server. This has broken deploys that otherwise looked healthy.

get_deployment RETURNS THE MERGED redu.md ONLY WHEN IT FITS ITS RESPONSE BUDGET. Over budget - which is normal for a mature recipe or any large app - it withholds redu_md_markdown and returns redu_md_last_deploy_block plus redu_md_deploy_log_line instead. That is NOT an error and must not be retried: apply those two edits to the file on disk and change nothing else.

⛔ THE MERGE NEVER WRITES A NEW QUIRK. Whatever redu returns, it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Every gotcha YOUR run discovered has to be typed into the quirks list by hand before you commit, or it is lost - and that list is the only part of the file that makes the next deploy cheaper.
⛔ NEVER WRITE A CREDENTIAL INTO redu.md. It is committed and read by the next person and the next agent. Names of variables, yes; their values, never. Hand secrets to the user in the session instead.

plan_deploy OVER-SIZES A PULLED COMPOSE STACK. Measured 8 times out of 8: declaring needs_compose makes it quote m1.large, roughly double the real requirement, because it cannot see that the images are pulled rather than built. Show the user the plan, but size from the app's real memory figure when you have one.

THE MANAGED DATABASE PASSWORD IS ON THE VM, NOT IN THE API. list_databases returns private_ip, port, db_name and db_user and DELIBERATELY NOT the password, so an agent that looks for it there finds nothing and starts guessing. The deploy writes the whole connection set into the compose project's .env on the app VM. Call get_env_keys for the NAMES first (no SSH, values never leave the VM); only if you need an actual VALUE, SSH in (get_ssh_command) and read that one key, `sudo grep '^PGPASSWORD=' /opt/app-src/.env`. ⚠️ That file is chmod 600 root:root so it needs sudo, and the database is on the PRIVATE network - reachable from the app VM, never from a laptop.

YOU CAN READ A DEPLOY VM WITHOUT SSHING INTO IT, and four tools do it: get_containers (what is running, health, restarts, crashed ones included), get_container_logs (what the app actually printed - the tool for 'deployed fine but does not work'), get_resource_usage (memory, disk, load, OOM kills) and get_env_keys (which variables got wired, by name). ⛔ get_instance_logs is the SERIAL CONSOLE and is not your app's logs; build_log stops when the build does. SSH is still yours for everything else - a shell on a real machine is the point, not a fallback.

⛔ THE PRIMARY SURFACE'S HOSTNAME COMES FROM THE TOP-LEVEL dname, NOT FROM expose[0].dname, WHICH IS SILENTLY DISCARDED. Extra expose entries DO keep the dname you give them, so the two behave differently and nothing tells you. If an app bakes its own public URL into config at boot (CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN, allowed_origins, SITE_URL), generate the full `<label>-<8 lowercase letters/digits>.redu.cloud` form yourself and pass it as the TOP-LEVEL dname, which is used verbatim. Passing it on expose[0] instead gets you an app configured for a hostname redu never created, answering 200 on a name it does not believe is its own.

WEBSOCKETS WORK THROUGH THE PROXY WITH NO CONFIGURATION: every proxy host redu creates has upgrade enabled. Measured at the protocol level, HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols with the subprotocol echoed back. ⚠️ TEST IT WITH `curl --http1.1`: plain curl negotiates HTTP/2, which has no Upgrade mechanism at all, so the app answers as an ordinary GET and the failure looks exactly like a proxy refusing to upgrade. Browsers use HTTP/1.1 for websockets regardless. Do not disable an app's realtime features on the strength of an HTTP/2 curl.

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/eikek/docspell
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghcr.io/docspell/restserver:v0.43.0 (plus ghcr.io/docspell/joex:v0.43.0)
  port: 7880
  vm: m1.large
  flavor_id: "4"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.066
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: docspell
quirks:
  - "READ THE DISK NUMBERS TO THE USER BEFORE YOU SIZE ANYTHING, BECAUSE DOCSPELL PUTS THE DOCUMENTS IN THE DATABASE. files.default-store defaults to database in BOTH components. Every scanned PDF, converted PDF/A, preview image and archived original is stored as blobs in the managed Postgres, NOT on the app VM. The MANAGED DATABASE flavor's disk is your archive size cap. m1.small gives 20 GB, m1.medium 40 GB, m1.large 80 GB. Budget two to three times the raw scan size."
  - "THE COMPOSE IS IN A DIFFERENT REPO. eikek/docspell contains only tools/exim/docker-compose.yml, an exim mail relay. The real stack is docspell/docker at docker-compose/docker-compose.yml. Adapt THAT one and delete three of its five services."
  - "WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY. Docspell has no instance administrator account. Every sign-up creates a COLLECTIVE, and backend.signup.mode defaults to open. Set DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_SIGNUP_MODE=invite and DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_SIGNUP_NEW__INVITE__PASSWORD BEFORE first boot. Then POST the invite password to /api/v1/open/signup/newinvite and register via /api/v1/open/signup/register. Do NOT use mode=closed to be safe: it refuses you too."
  - "IS REGISTRATION OPEN AFTER YOUR ACCOUNT EXISTS? In invite mode, only to somebody holding a key you minted; keys are single-use, 3 day validity. Belt-and-braces is to redeploy with mode=closed. Ask the user which they want."
  - "DO NOT COPY THE ADMIN SECRET OUT OF THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE. It is a published value that unlocks password reset for every account. The default in reference.conf is EMPTY, which disables every /api/v1/admin route, and empty is what this recipe ships."
  - "DISABLE THE INTEGRATION ENDPOINT, WHICH THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE TURNS ON. POST /api/v1/open/integration/item/<collective> is anonymous by design and the header protecting it is published. Set it to false and drop the consumedir container."
  - "DELETE THREE OF THE FIVE UPSTREAM SERVICES: db (bundled postgres), consumedir (bind-mounts ./docs, feeds the disabled integration endpoint), solr. What remains is restserver and joex."
  - "SOLR CAN BE DROPPED WITHOUT LOSING FULL-TEXT SEARCH. Set on BOTH components FULL__TEXT__SEARCH_ENABLED=true, FULL__TEXT__SEARCH_BACKEND=postgresql and FULL__TEXT__SEARCH_POSTGRESQL_USE__DEFAULT__CONNECTION=true. Creates one table plus a GIN index, no extension needed. Removes a third JVM and a second stateful volume."
  - "THE FULL-TEXT CONFIG MUST BE IDENTICAL ON BOTH COMPONENTS. Setting it on the restserver only gives a search box that returns nothing, because joex writes the index, and nothing errors."
  - "WITHOUT THE JDBC VARIABLES BOTH CONTAINERS COME UP HEALTHY ON SEPARATE THROWAWAY H2 DATABASES IN /tmp. Set all three on EACH component. deploy_compose with database:managed only APPENDS PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/DATABASE_URL to the project .env, so the compose must interpolate them itself. Docspell does NOT read DATABASE_URL."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. docker exec docspell-restserver printenv DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL must print a jdbc:postgresql:// url at the private database IP; THEN docker exec docspell-restserver ls /tmp must show NO docspell-demo.db. Repeat for joex."
  - "SET DOCSPELL_SERVER_AUTH_SERVER__SECRET EXPLICITLY AND REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY. It ships EMPTY and a random one is generated when empty, so every restart invalidates every session and remember-me token."
  - "BOTH COMPONENTS BIND TO localhost BY DEFAULT. Set DOCSPELL_SERVER_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0 and DOCSPELL_JOEX_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0."
  - "THE TWO CONTAINERS HAVE TO FIND EACH OTHER. DOCSPELL_SERVER_INTERNAL__URL=http://docspell-restserver:7880 and DOCSPELL_JOEX_BASE__URL=http://docspell-joex:7878. Wrong url looks like extreme slowness, not a misconfiguration."
  - "DO NOT PUBLISH joex's PORT 7878. It is a small unauthenticated HTTP API for inspecting and cancelling jobs. Expose ONLY the restserver's 7880."
  - "SET DOCSPELL_SERVER_BASE__URL TO THE PUBLIC HTTPS ORIGIN, AND GENERATE THE DNAME YOURSELF FIRST in the full docspell-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form."
  - "A HEALTHY DOCSPELL ANSWERS 303 ON /, NOT 200. Use GET /api/info/version, which is anonymous and returns JSON containing builtAtString."
  - "GIVE joex AN EXPLICIT HEAP. Upstream says -Xmx1400M at least at nlp.mode=full. Add command: [-J-Xmx1400M] to the joex service."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE. m1.large reasons from joex at 1400M plus a second JVM, a resident LibreOffice listener, and ghostscript/tesseract/ocrmypdf subprocesses. m1.medium (4 GB) is NOT enough. Measure it on your run."
  - "EXPECT A SLOW FIRST BOOT. v0.43.0 manifests list 1976.3 MB of compressed layers for joex and 409.3 MB for restserver, then Flyway migrations. Use created_at and the dated last line of build_log, not poll counts."
  - "ONE DATABASE, NO SUPERUSER, NO EXTENSIONS. Docspell creates its own tables with Flyway; the PostgreSQL fts backend adds one table in the SAME database. db_superuser is not needed."
  - "NO VOLUME IS REQUIRED ON THE APP VM. Neither container holds state; joex's working directories are scratch under /tmp. Everything that matters is in the managed Postgres."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> generate the dname and set DOCSPELL_SERVER_BASE__URL -> generate the auth server secret and the signup invite password -> plan_deploy -> show the user the plan, the cost and THE TWO DISK NUMBERS, then WAIT -> deploy_compose with flavor_id 4, database managed, db_engine postgres, db_flavor_id 2, port 7880 -> run the check script -> mint one invite key and register the user's account."
  - "THIS IS ABOVE THE NO-CARD TRIAL CEILING, WHICH IS m1.medium FOR THE VM AND m1.small FOR THE ONE MANAGED DATABASE. Say it BEFORE the plan is approved, and do not quietly drop to m1.medium."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Assemble the trimmed two-service compose locally, then prepare_upload -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "plan_deploy WILL WANT TO UPSIZE ONCE needs_compose IS DECLARED. m1.large happens to be right for Docspell anyway. Make sure the DATABASE flavor is the one you chose."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0-or-later. awesome-selfhosted says GPL-3.0 and is wrong. AGPL section 13 applies to the USER only if they MODIFY Docspell and let others use it over a network."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, AND HERE THAT MEANS THE WHOLE ARCHIVE. delete_deployment keeps the managed Postgres and keeps billing GBP 0.0174/hr. delete_database deletes every document. delete_database has twice timed out at the MCP layer while succeeding server-side: confirm with list_databases rather than retrying."
---

# Self-host Docspell on redu

Scan a pile of paper into one searchable archive that you own: OCR, automatic tagging and
full-text search, on your own VM, with the documents in a managed Postgres beside it.

## What this deploys

- Docspell restserver from the official pinned image, on one m1.large VM, port 7880.
- Docspell joex, the worker that does OCR, PDF conversion and text analysis, on the same VM
  and not exposed to the internet.
- Managed Postgres on its own private VM, holding the metadata, the full-text index and the
  document files themselves.
- A public hostname on *.redu.cloud with TLS.

About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. Above the no-card trial ceiling.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed.

content.text:
Plan written to `redu-deploy-plan.md`. Here it is.

## Docspell on redu — the plan

**Two containers on one VM, documents in a managed Postgres beside it.**

| | |
|---|---|
| App VM | **m1.large** — 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 80 GB — £0.0486/hr |
| Managed Postgres | **m1.small** — 1 vCPU / 2 GB / **20 GB** — £0.0174/hr |
| **Total** | **£0.066/hr ≈ £48.18/month** |
| URL | `https://docspell-y2i0rckx.redu.cloud` (generated up front, baked into the config) |

Fits your quota (needs 2 instances / 5 vCPU / 10 GB; you have 10 / 20 / 50 GB free). **This is above the no-card trial ceiling** (m1.medium VM + m1.small DB), so it needs a payment method on the account. I won't quietly shrink the VM to make it fit — joex alone wants 1400 MB of heap and a 4 GB box would thrash under OCR.

### ⚠️ The disk number to decide on now

**Docspell stores the document files in the database, not on the VM.** Every scan, its converted PDF, and its preview images are blobs in Postgres. So the **database flavor's disk is your archive size cap** — and the app VM's 80 GB holds only Ubuntu, Docker and the two images.

| Managed Postgres | Disk | Total £/hr | Total £/mo |
|---|---|---|---|
| **m1.small** (planned) | **20 GB** | 0.066 | 48.18 |
| m1.medium | 40 GB | 0.0764 | 55.77 |
| m1.large | 80 GB | 0.0972 | 70.96 |

Budget **2–3× your raw scan size** — original + converted PDF + previews are all kept. Growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy.

### What I changed from upstream's compose

Upstream ships five services with published secrets in them. This ships two:

- **Dropped `db`** (managed Postgres instead), **`solr`** (full-text index goes into that same Postgres — saves a third JVM), **`consumedir`** (only existed to feed the integration endpoint).
- **Admin secret → empty.** Upstream's `admin123` is a published string that lets anyone reset any account's password. Empty disables the `/api/v1/admin` routes entirely.
- **Integration endpoint → off.** Upstream turns on an anonymous upload endpoint protected by a header value printed in every tutorial.
- **Signup → `invite`** with a generated password, set *before first boot*. The default is `open`, and Docspell has **no instance administrator** — anyone who found the URL could create their own tenant and there'd be no way to evict them.
- **joex's port 7878 not published** (it's an unauthenticated job-control API), and given an explicit `-J-Xmx1400M`.

Nothing is built — both images are pulled and pinned at `v0.43.0`. Expect a slow first boot: ~2.4 GB of compressed layers, because joex carries every Tesseract language pack, LibreOffice and Ghostscript.

content.text: Provisioning. Managed Postgres `docspell` (db #150) is wired. While the layers pull, let me stage the verification script from the recipe.

input.command:
cat > verify-docspell.sh <<'VEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a fresh Docspell is not open for registration.
#   ./verify-docspell.sh docspell-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = NOT closed, 2 = inconclusive (retry; it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-docspell.sh <host>.redu.cloud}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. Everything below is vacuous unless Docspell itself is answering.
#    Note / is a 303 to /app on a HEALTHY instance, so this uses the JSON endpoint instead.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/info/version" || echo 000)
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info/version answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ]; then
    echo "  That is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"builtAtString"' "$TMP/ver"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200, but the body is not Docspell's VersionInfo." >&2
  echo "  Something else is answering on this hostname. Do not read this as closed." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK   Docspell is answering: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL for step 3. A route that exists but rejects the method answers 405;
#    a route that is not registered answers 404. Without this, a moved endpoint would make
#    step 3 pass for the wrong reason.
probe=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
if [ "$probe" != "405" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: GET on the register route answered $probe, expected 405." >&2
  echo "  The signup API has moved. Step 3 would prove nothing. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK   the register route is where this recipe expects it (GET -> 405)"

# 3. THE NEGATIVE, and it means something now: a registration with no invite key is refused.
probe_name="probe$(date +%s)"
probe_pw=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)

content.text:
The cleanup was blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier, so I've stopped rather than trying to route around it. Here's where things stand and what I need from you.

## What happened

The deploy failed, on redu's side, not in the Docspell config:

- **Deployment 461** — app VM `docspell` (m1.large) is **ACTIVE but in terminal `error`/`failed` state**, running zero containers. It is billing **£0.0486/hr for nothing**.
- **Managed Postgres db #150** — status `error`, **no VM was ever created**. Redu tried twice (two orphaned 20 GB volumes at 14:22:54 and 14:22:58, never attached), and both instances failed to boot.
- This was **not** a quota wall — instances, RAM and volumes were all comfortably under limit at that moment. It looks like a scheduler or host-side failure. Three other databases in your account created in the same minute came up fine.

Nothing was lost: no containers ever started, so there was never any data. The compose itself is fine and validated.

One useful confirmation from the wreckage: the VM's `.env` ended up with `PGUSER`, `PGPASSWORD`, `PGDATABASE` but **no `PGHOST` or `PGPORT`** — so the JDBC URL would have interpolated to `jdbc:postgresql://:/docspell`. The recipe's insistence on proving that wiring in both directions is well founded.

## What I need to do next

To retry I have to remove the failed deployment first — redu can't re-point a dead deployment at a new database, and the hostname `docspell-y2i0rckx.redu.cloud` is baked into `DOCSPELL_SERVER_BASE__URL`, so I want to reuse it.

Now the picture is clear, and the recipe's step 2 is simply wrong for this stack:

- `POST /api/v1/open/signup/register` → `{"success":false,"message":"Invalid invitation key."}` — **invite mode is working**.
- `GET` on *every* POST-only route (`register`, `newinvite`, `auth/login`) → **404**, identical to a nonexistent path.

http4s returns 404 on method mismatch, not 405 — so the recipe's positive control can never pass against Docspell, and as written it would condemn a perfectly good instance. Rewriting it around a control that actually discriminates:

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("verify-docspell.sh")
s = p.read_text()

old_start = s.index("# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL for step 3.")
old_end   = s.index('echo\necho "Still to do on the VM')
new = '''# 2+3. POSITIVE CONTROL AND NEGATIVE, IN ONE REQUEST.
#    ⚠️ The original recipe probed GET on the register route and expected 405. Docspell is
#    http4s, and http4s falls through to 404 on a method mismatch -- GET on register,
#    newinvite and auth/login ALL answer 404, exactly like a path that does not exist. So a
#    405 control can never pass, and would condemn a healthy instance. Measured 2026-08-18.
#    The control that DOES discriminate: POST the registration and require Docspell's own
#    JSON envelope back. A moved/absent route gives 404 and no "success" field; a live one
#    gives 200 and a verdict. That makes the refusal below mean something.
probe_name="probe$(date +%s)"
probe_pw=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)
code=$(printf '{"collectiveName":"%s","login":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \\
        "$probe_name" "$probe_name" "$probe_pw" \\
      | curl -sS -o "$TMP/reg" -w '%{http_code}' -H 'content-type: application/json' \\
             --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q '"success"' "$TMP/reg"; then
  echo "FAIL: POST to the register route answered $code with body: $(cat "$TMP/reg")" >&2
  echo "  Expected 200 and Docspell's JSON envelope. The signup API has moved;" >&2
  echo "  a refusal here would prove nothing. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK   the register route is live and answering Docspell JSON (POST -> 200 + \\"success\\")"

out=$(cat "$TMP/reg")
case "$out" in
  *'"success":false'*'nvitation key'*)
    # invite mode specifically: 'closed' would refuse with a different message, and
    # 'open' would return success:true and create a tenant.
    echo "OK   anonymous signup refused, and refused for the INVITE-mode reason: $out" ;;
  *'"success":false'*)
    echo "OK   anonymous signup refused: $out"
    echo "WARN the refusal is not the invite-key message; check signup mode is 'invite' not 'closed'." >&2 ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL: anonymous signup was NOT refused: $out" >&2
    echo "  Signup mode is not 'invite'. Anyone who finds this URL can create a tenant on it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

'''
p.write_text(s[:old_start] + new + s[old_end:])
print("rewrote steps 2-3")

# 2+3. POSITIVE CONTROL AND NEGATIVE, IN ONE REQUEST.
#    ⚠️ The original recipe probed GET on the register route and expected 405. Docspell is
#    http4s, and http4s falls through to 404 on a method mismatch -- GET on register,
#    newinvite and auth/login ALL answer 404, exactly like a path that does not exist. So a
#    405 control can never pass, and would condemn a healthy instance. Measured 2026-08-18.

#    JSON envelope back. A moved/absent route gives 404 and no "success" field; a live one

probe_name="probe$(date +%s)"
probe_pw=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)
code=$(printf '{"collectiveName":"%s","login":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
        "$probe_name" "$probe_name" "$probe_pw" \
      | curl -sS -o "$TMP/reg" -w '%{http_code}' -H 'content-type: application/json' \

if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q '"success"' "$TMP/reg"; then
  echo "FAIL: POST to the register route answered $code with body: $(cat "$TMP/reg")" >&2
  echo "  Expected 200 and Docspell's JSON envelope. The signup API has moved;" >&2
  echo "  a refusal here would prove nothing. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi

content.text:
Docspell is live and verified end to end.

**https://docspell-y2i0rckx.redu.cloud**

| | |
|---|---|
| Login | `milos` |
| Password | `«REDACTED:entropy:a763fc82»` |
| Collective | `milos` |
| Invite password | `«REDACTED:entropy:992c980a»` — POST to `/api/v1/open/signup/newinvite` to mint a key for anyone else |

Change the password in the UI when you're in. Signup stays in **invite** mode as you chose — nobody can register without a single-use key you mint. The auth server secret is pinned in `docker-compose.yml`, so restarts won't log you out; reuse that file on any redeploy.

**Cost: £0.066/hr ≈ £48.18/month** — m1.large app VM (£0.0486) + m1.small managed Postgres (£0.0174). Your 20 GB database disk is the archive cap; budget 2–3× your raw scan size, and resize the volume when you approach it.

### Verified, not assumed

Both containers running with zero restarts; both JDBC URLs point at `[ip]:5432/docspell`, matching the database's real private IP, and neither `/tmp` holds `docspell-demo.db`. Full-text config is `postgresql` on **both** components. Admin secret empty, integration endpoint off, joex's 7878 unpublished. I uploaded a test PDF: it processed in under 30 s, converted to PDF/A, and came back from `content:widgets` and `content:acme` — words present only inside the file — while a nonsense term returned nothing. Then I deleted it; your archive is empty.

### Two things went wrong, and both are now recorded

**The first deploy failed.** Redu's managed Postgres errored during provisioning — no VM was ever created, so the app VM hung in `waiting-db` and went terminal. Not a quota wall; three other databases in your account came up fine in the same minute. The tell was `.env` carrying `PGUSER`/`PGPASSWORD`/`PGDATABASE` but no `PGHOST`, which would have produced `jdbc:postgresql://:/docspell`. I tore it down, deleted two orphaned 20 GB volumes it leaked, and retried with no changes — the retry worked. Total time lost, ~20 minutes; you were billed for an idle m1.large during it.

**Two claims in `redu.md` were wrong, and I've corrected them in the file:**

- The check script's positive control expected **405** on `GET /api/v1/open/signup/register`. Docspell is http4s, which falls through to **404** on a method mismatch — `register`, `newinvite` and `auth/login` all answer 404, same as a nonexistent path. That control could never pass; it failed against a perfectly healthy instance. I replaced it with one that discriminates: POST the registration and require HTTP 200 plus Docspell's JSON envelope, then assert the refusal names the invitation key (which distinguishes `invite` from `closed`).
- The file said `delete_database` always succeeds behind its MCP timeout. The first call timed out and had genuinely **not** deleted; the second timed out and had. Confirm with `list_databases` after every attempt.

### Files in your project

`redu.md` (7 new quirks, pinned dname, real measurements, corrected script), `redu-deploy-plan.md` (real deployed values, replacing the estimate), `verify-docspell.sh` (re-runnable, exits 0), `docker-compose.yml` (exactly what's deployed). The first three are secret-free; **`docker-compose.yml` contains the auth secret and invite password** by design, so don't commit it publicly.

Measured for the next run: **7 min 54 s** deploy-to-healthy, and steady state of **2090 MB of 7941** with joex at 1.21 GiB — m1.large is comfortable, and the m1.medium warning holds on joex alone.

To stop paying entirely you need **both** `delete_deployment(463)` and `delete_database(152)` — and the second one deletes every document, since Docspell stores files in the database.
